text:
marie: Quick perf note from running FP8 rollout smoke on staging: seeing ~8-15% tail regressions on some A100 nodes (sm80) when CUTLASS FP8 kernels are enabled. stack: triton -> cutlass fp8 path. repro profile attached below.

sanjay: can you paste the perf numbers and which models/seq len?

marie: model=falcon-7b, seq=2048/4096 samples, warmup=200. summary:
```
baseline (INT8 optimized): p50=42ms p95=110ms p99=230ms
with CUTLASS-FP8: p50=38ms p95=125ms p99=265ms
delta: p99 +15%-+16% on a subset of hosts (sm80). sm90 hosts unaffected (~-5% in p95).
```
note: KV cache hit rate was ~60% during test (cold-ish).

bob: interesting — p50 down but tails worse. smells like calibration noise + kernel fallback jitter. any logs showing which kernel variants were chosen?

marie: paste from runtime tracing:
```
[2025-09-12T13:04:12Z] kernel_select: CUTLASS_FP8_sm80 fwd_k=fp8_eigen_v2
[2025-09-12T13:04:12Z] kernel_select: fallback -> CUTLASS_INT8_sm80_conv (after 3 failed launches)
[2025-09-12T13:04:12Z] kvcache: miss_ratio=0.42 warmup_seq=128
```
looks like some launches hit NUM_RETRY path and then fallback to INT8 which costs extra latency.

alice: calibration looks suspect. when we calibrated FP8 we used a small calibration set and per-tensor scales; distribution tail can push quant ranges and trigger slower kernels (atomic paths). can we compute calibration stdev at runtime? if stdev>0.6 route to INT8/4bit fallback for the first N requests.

chris: also seeing batching heuristics amplify this: large dynamic batches while KV cache cold create variable shapes and extra kernel switches. suggestion: keep batch_multiplier capped during first 30s after model load or post-rollback.

marie: proposal:
- detect arch at startup (cudaDeviceGetAttribute(GPU_ARCH_SM) or nvml query) and set kernel whitelist per-arch. allow FP8 only on sm90 by default.
- runtime calibration check: compute per-layer scale mean/std on first K calibration batches; if std>THRESH, mark layer as "unstable" and route to INT8 for that layer for first M inferences.
- change batching: small-batch warmup (batch<=2) for first 10s or until KV cache hit rate >80%.
- build flag note: need CUTLASS compiled with multi-arch targets and FP8_ENABLE + FP8_FALLBACK macro to avoid runtime link errors on sm80 when kernel not present.

sanjay: +1. two questions: 1) what's a safe THRESH value? 2) will per-layer routing cost more overhead?

bob: THRESH: empirical from experiments => scale_std/scale_mean > 0.25 correlated with tail regressions. per-layer routing cost ~= 0.5-1ms bookkeeping, still cheaper than repeated fallback penalties.

marie: here's a quick pseudo patch (runtime kernel router):
```
if (arch >= SM90 && calibration_ok(layer)) {
  use_kernel(FP8_FAST);
} else if (layer_unstable(layer)) {
  use_kernel(INT8_STABLE);
} else {
  use_kernel(DEFAULT);
}
```
we'll also add a `--batch-warmup` env var (default 10s) and `CUTLASS_BUILD_TARGETS="sm80;sm90"` to the buildkite job.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Perf checks queued: nightly/rt-perf-sm80 and nightly/rt-perf-sm90. see: https://ci.redwood/inference/jobs/rt-perf-1750

chris: OK to land non-invasive bits (arch detection + env flags + batch cap) behind feature-flag. leave calibration router behind feature-flag until we have more runs.

marie: plan: I'll open PR with arch detection + envs + batch warmup today, add telemetry for scale_std and kernel selection events, then we run two-nightly perf jobs before enabling calibration router.

bob: I'll run a quick A/B on dedicated hosts (sm80 pool) after your PR.

sanjay: thanks — add me on the PR for reviews.

marie: filing TODOs: PR, perf runs, CUTLASS rebuild with multi-arch FP8 flags, update release notes. :thumbsup:
